lines.text: London stank so bad, Parliament had to act.

parts.tts: London stank so bad, Parliament had to act.
parts.heard: London stank so bad, Parliament had to act.

lines.text: Summer 1858. A heatwave hit the Thames.

parts.tts: Summer eighteen fifty-eight. A heatwave hit the Thames.
parts.heard: Summer, 1858. A heatwave hit the Thames.

lines.text: And the Thames... was full of London's sewage.
Parliament sits right on the river.

parts.tts: Parliament sits right on the river.
parts.heard: Parliament sits right on the river.

lines.text: So they soaked the curtains with chemicals.

parts.tts: So they soaked the curtains with chemicals.
parts.heard: So they soaked the curtains with chemicals.

lines.text: They even talked about moving Parliament out of London.

parts.tts: They even talked about moving Parliament out of London.
parts.heard: They even talked about moving Parliament out of London.

lines.text: Instead, they passed a new sewer law in about seven weeks.

parts.tts: Instead, they passed a new sewer law in about seven weeks.
parts.heard: Instead, they passed a new sewer law in about seven weeks.

lines.text: Engineer Joseph Bazalgette built 82 miles of giant sewers.
